condition.notes: Desktop ATX 5VSB missing. 5VSB is the first desktop rail; without it the board will not respond to the power button.

next_steps.action: Unplug the PSU from mains. Wait 60 s for the 5VSB bulk cap to bleed. Measure resistance from the 5VSB pin (pin 9 of the 24-pin ATX, purple wire) to ground.

measure.where: Pin 9 of the 24-pin ATX connector (purple wire) or the 5VSB test point on the board
measure.instrument: DMM resistance mode (200 ohm then 2 kohm)
measure.expected: Typically >100 ohm on a healthy board. <10 ohm indicates a shorted 5VSB load (super-IO, EC, wake-on-LAN PHY, RTC backup diode).
measure.safety: Unplug from mains and wait for the 5VSB bulk cap to discharge. The 5VSB rail is always live when the PSU is plugged in.

interpretations.then: Short on the 5VSB load. The PSU will shut down 5VSB to protect itself. Hunt the shorted component (super-IO, EC, WOL PHY) before re-applying mains.

No short on the motherboard. Re-plug mains and measure 5VSB at the ATX connector. If 5VSB is absent at the connector, the PSU is faulty. If present at the connector but missing on the board, the 24-pin connector or the board's 5VSB input fuse is open.
